title: Positive part sum equals half the $\ell^1$ norm
statement:
Let $a\colon\alpha\to\bbr$ be a real-valued function on a finite type $\alpha$ whose values sum to zero, that is, $\sum_{x\in\alpha} a(x) = 0$. Then the sum of the positive parts of $a$ equals half the sum of its absolute values:
\[
\sum_{x\in\alpha} \max\bigl(a(x),\,0\bigr) \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\sum_{x\in\alpha} \abs{a(x)}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: the values of $a$ sum to zero
replaced:
Let $a : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function on a finite type with $\sum_x a(x) = 0$.
Then $\sum_x \max(a(x), 0) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_x |a(x)|$.
